territorial_scope.description: Applies to Connecticut state agencies, the Judicial Department and state contracting agencies, and to businesses contracting with them.

evidence.quote: no state agency shall implement any system that employs artificial intelligence

summary.short: Connecticut Public Act 23-16 requires state agencies and the Judicial Department to inventory and assess AI systems for unlawful discrimination, bars agencies from deploying AI without a prior impact assessment from February 1, 2024, requires state contracts to include data privacy compliance clauses, and creates an AI working group.
summary.long: Public Act No. 23-16 (Substitute Senate Bill 1103) governs artificial intelligence (AI) systems used by Connecticut state agencies and the Judicial Department. Sections 1 and 3 require the Department of Administrative Services and the Judicial Department to inventory their AI systems annually, publish the inventories, and assess the systems for unlawful discrimination or disparate impact. Section 2 requires the Office of Policy and Management to establish policies and procedures for state agency AI systems, including a pre-implementation impact assessment, and bars state agencies from implementing such a system without that assessment or where the agency head determines it will cause unlawful discrimination or disparate impact, from February 1, 2024. Section 3(d) applies similar limits to the Judicial Department. Section 4, effective October 1, 2023, requires state contracting agencies to include in business contracts a clause requiring compliance with sections 42-515 to 42-525 of the general statutes. Section 5 creates a legislative working group on AI in state government, which must report by February 1, 2024. The text states no penalties or enforcement mechanism.

notes: Enrolled text of Public Act 23-16, approved June 7, 2023. Sec. 1-3 are effective July 1, 2023, Sec. 4 October 1, 2023, and Sec. 5 from passage. The 'artificial intelligence' definition appears in Sec. 1, 2, 3 and 5 in slightly different wording and structure. Sec. 1(c) and Sec. 5(b)(2) refer internally to Sec. 2 of this act (not coded as relations). Sec. 1(b)(1) sets an inventory deadline of December 31, 2023, while Sec. 1(c) starts assessments on February 1, 2024. The general statutes cited are not reproduced in the document, so their content is not verified here.

thresholds.note: Reviewed all sections. The dates (July 1 2023, October 1 2023, December 31 2023, February 1 2024) are effective dates and procedural deadlines, which are events rather than thresholds. The fifty per cent quorum in Sec. 5(c)(1)(D) is a procedural voting rule for the working group, not a scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation-tier or penalty cutoff. No numeric threshold changing legal treatment was found.
